name: Valley Spring Recovery Center
summary: Valley Spring Recovery Center holds dual New Jersey licenses for substance use and mental health treatment, publishes its program schedules, and runs an evening intensive outpatient track built around people who are still working.

spec.Levels of care: Partial care, IOP, evening IOP, outpatient, telehealth
spec.Licensing: NJ SUD #200887 and NJ mental health #70420104
spec.Notable: First responder program; case management and return-to-work support; alumni network

verdict: Our preferred overall option for structured care with a real mental health license. Both license numbers are published, which is rare in this market and easy to verify. A specialized program for first responders, health and wellness programming, and a robust alumni network that brings in motivational speakers—pro wrestler Zack Clayton and Kendrick Perkins, the former NBA champion, have both appeared. Substantial return-to-work and case management credentials alongside licensed clinical and medical staff. Confirm current openings and which payers are in network for your specific plan.

Clinical clarity: Program schedules are published with actual times rather than described in the abstract, and the levels of care are distinguished from one another rather than blurred into one offering.
Medical support: Medical director and psychiatric prescribing are named as part of the program. There is no on-site detox, so withdrawal management is arranged elsewhere — ask how that handoff is handled.
Program depth: Partial care through outpatient, plus specialty tracks for first responders and working professionals, family programming, case management and health and wellness.
Continuing care: An active alumni program with regular events, plus case management and return-to-work support extending past discharge.

fits: Someone whose primary problem is mental health rather than substance use, since the standalone mental health license means no substance use diagnosis is required
People who cannot stop working and need an evening intensive outpatient schedule
First responders looking for a program built for them
Anyone who wants to verify credentials before calling — both license numbers are published
notFits: Anyone likely to need medically supervised withdrawal, which is not provided on site
People needing residential or inpatient care
Adolescents — this is an adult program
ask: Which of the two licenses would my admission fall under, and does that change the schedule?
What are the exact start and end times of the evening IOP, and what happens if I miss a session for work?
If detox turns out to be necessary, who provides it and who holds clinical responsibility during it?
Is my specific plan in network, and what is the expected out-of-pocket figure in writing?

name: ChoicePoint
summary: An outpatient program with unusually specific published detail on medication-assisted treatment, and one of the few in this group stating it accepts Medicare and Medicaid.

spec.Notable: Names specific medications; accepts Medicare and Medicaid

verdict: Best documented for medication-assisted treatment and the strongest option here on public insurance access. There is no residential level, so confirm the plan if withdrawal management beyond outpatient is likely.

Clinical clarity: Therapies are named specifically — cognitive behavioral therapy, dialectical behavior therapy and EMDR — rather than gestured at.
Medical support: The strongest medication detail in this group. Buprenorphine, methadone and naltrexone are named for opioid use, acamprosate and disulfiram for alcohol. Outpatient detox is offered.
Program depth: A clear outpatient ladder with telehealth and dual diagnosis care, but no partial care, residential or inpatient level.
Continuing care: Relapse prevention support is described. Alumni structure is not detailed publicly.

fits: People on Medicare or Medicaid, who have very few options in this group
Anyone whose treatment will center on medication for opioid or alcohol use disorder
People who want care delivered partly or wholly by telehealth
notFits: Anyone needing residential care or a full-day partial care program
People whose withdrawal risk exceeds what an outpatient setting can manage safely
ask: Which state license do you hold, and what is its number and expiration date?
Is outpatient detox appropriate for my specific substance and history, or do I need an inpatient setting?
Which medication would you expect to start with, and who prescribes and monitors it?
How many hours per week is the intensive outpatient program?

name: BlueCrest Recovery Center
summary: The most complete ladder in this group, running from medical detox through residential and down to outpatient, with a stated 12-step and holistic model.

spec.Levels of care: Medical detox, residential, partial care, IOP, outpatient, aftercare
spec.Notable: Does not accept Medicaid or Medicare

verdict: Best fit when the full continuum matters and someone may need to start at detox and step down without changing providers. The 12-step emphasis suits people who want it and is worth discussing if you do not. Private insurance only.

Clinical clarity: The model is stated clearly as integrating clinical, spiritual and holistic methods with 12-step principles. Session-level scheduling detail is thinner.
Medical support: Medical detox is delivered in house rather than referred out, which removes the most common point of failure in a treatment episode.
Program depth: The only center in this group offering the entire ladder from medical detox through residential to outpatient and aftercare under one provider.
Continuing care: Aftercare and alumni services are named as a distinct part of the offering.

fits: Someone who may need detox and wants to step down through levels without changing providers
People who want or are open to a 12-step framework
Anyone who values a stack of third-party accreditations
notFits: People on Medicaid or Medicare, which the center states it does not accept
Anyone specifically seeking a non-12-step approach
People whose primary problem is mental health rather than substance use
ask: What is your state license number and expiration date?
How long is the typical detox stay, and what determines the move to residential?
How central is the 12-step component, and what is offered to someone who does not want it?
Since Medicaid and Medicare are not accepted, what is the self-pay rate per level of care?

name: North Jersey Recovery Center
summary: Publishes two distinct tracks, one for mental health and one for substance use, and lists an evening intensive outpatient option alongside the standard daytime schedule.

spec.Levels of care: Partial care, IOP, evening IOP, outpatient, MAT
spec.Notable: PPO and POS plans; does not accept Medicaid

verdict: A reasonable option for working schedules with a clearly separated mental health track. No accreditation or license detail is published, so ask for the license number and its expiration date before you commit.

Clinical clarity: The separation of the mental health and substance use tracks is stated explicitly, and the mental health conditions treated are listed by name.
Medical support: Medication-assisted treatment is offered. Detail on prescribing staff and medical oversight is limited publicly.
Program depth: Partial care down through outpatient, with a separately listed evening intensive outpatient option.
Continuing care: Less publicly documented than the rest of the offering.

fits: People who need an evening schedule and want a mental health track that is genuinely separate
Anyone stepping down from a higher level of care elsewhere
Commercial PPO and POS plan holders
notFits: Anyone who needs on-site detox or residential care
People who want to see accreditation before making contact — none is published
ask: What is your state license number and expiration date, and are you accredited by CARF or The Joint Commission?
Does the mental health track have its own license, or does admission require a substance use diagnosis?
What are the evening IOP hours?
What does aftercare look like once the program ends?

name: Boca Recovery Center — Englewood
summary: The Northern New Jersey site of a multi-state operator, listing medical detox, mental health services and specialized trauma and eating disorder therapy alongside outpatient care.

spec.Levels of care: Medical detox, MAT, mental health services, outpatient
spec.Accreditation: Not published on the location page
spec.Notable: Also operates in Galloway and Ventnor City, NJ, plus FL, IN and MA

verdict: Worth a look for specialized therapy needs, particularly trauma and eating disorders, which few centers in this group name at all. Location-level program detail is thinner than the national pages suggest, so confirm what runs at Englewood specifically rather than company-wide.

Clinical clarity: Company-wide pages are detailed, but it is often unclear which services run at Englewood as opposed to another location in the group.
Medical support: Medical detox and medication-assisted treatment are both listed at the Englewood location.
Program depth: Specialized trauma and eating disorder therapy is named, which almost no other center in this group offers.
Continuing care: Multi-state footprint could support continuity across a relocation, but this is not described in detail.

fits: People who need trauma or eating disorder treatment alongside substance use care
Anyone who may need medical detox in Bergen County
People who might relocate and want a provider with sites in several states
notFits: Anyone who wants a single local program with everything documented at the address they will drive to
People who need to confirm accreditation before making contact
ask: Which of your listed services actually run at the Englewood location?
What is the license number for the Englewood site specifically?
Is the eating disorder program medically supervised, and at what level of care?
If I start at Englewood, where would I step down to?

name: IKON Recovery Centers
summary: A broad outpatient offering with several named specialty tracks and a published state license number, but detox is arranged through partners rather than delivered on site.

spec.Levels of care: Partial care, IOP, outpatient, MAT, telehealth
spec.Licensing: License 2000964, published with an expiration date
spec.Accreditation: The Joint Commission; LegitScript; NAADAC; NALGAP
spec.Notable: Executive, Heroes and Pride tracks; no in-house detox or sober living

verdict: Strong on published credentials, weakest on continuity. The site states plainly that detox and sober living are not provided in house, which means a handoff at the two points where handoffs fail most often. Ask exactly which partner handles withdrawal management and who holds clinical responsibility during it.

Clinical clarity: Specialty tracks are named and the license number is published with an expiration date, which is more transparency than most of this group offers.
Medical support: Medication-assisted treatment and Vivitrol are offered, but the site states detox is not provided in house and is arranged through partners.
Program depth: Partial care through outpatient, plus Executive, Heroes and Pride tracks and trauma-informed care.
Continuing care: Extended aftercare is emphasized, but the absence of in-house sober living removes a common step in the transition home.

fits: People who want a specialty track — executive, first responder or LGBTQ-focused
Anyone who wants to verify a license number before calling
People already stabilized who do not need withdrawal management
notFits: Anyone likely to need detox, which happens at a partner facility rather than here
People who want sober living attached to the program
Anyone who wants one provider responsible from withdrawal through aftercare
ask: Which facility handles detox, and who is clinically responsible during the transfer?
Is license 2000964 current, and has it been renewed past its stated expiration?
What does the Heroes track include that the standard program does not?
Where do clients go for sober living, and is that arrangement formal?
